tasks.question: Why do so many young people move to cities?

cues.cue: rural areas / offer / few job opportunities
models: This can largely be attributed to rural areas offering few job opportunities, which explains why young people leave.

cues.cue: cities / provide / better career prospects
models: One of the main causes of this is the fact that cities provide better career prospects, and this leads to a steady flow of young migrants.

cues.cue: young people / seek / more social opportunities
models: The root cause of this is that young people seek more social opportunities, which is why cities continue to attract them, and until this changes rural populations will keep shrinking.

cues.cue: universities / concentrate / in urban areas
models: This issue often stems from a lack of universities outside cities, which results in students relocating permanently.

cues.cue: small towns / lack / entertainment and culture
models: A major contributing factor is the way small towns lack entertainment and culture, and this has meant that young people feel drawn to city life.

cues.cue: wages / tend to be / higher in cities
models: This is mainly caused by wages tending to be higher in cities, which means that young people move to increase their earnings, and as a result rural areas lose talent.

tasks.question: Why is it difficult to learn a foreign language?

cues.cue: learners / get / little regular practice
models: This is primarily the result of learners getting little regular practice, which has led to slow progress, particularly in speaking skills.

cues.cue: grammar rules / differ / greatly from the learner's own language
models: This largely arises from the fact that grammar rules differ greatly from the learner's own language, making it difficult to build fluency quickly.

cues.cue: students / lack / exposure to native speakers
models: This issue often stems from a lack of exposure to native speakers, which results in weaker listening skills.

cues.cue: motivation / fades / without clear goals
models: This problem is frequently linked to motivation fading without clear goals, which suggests that structured targets are needed, and therefore progress often stalls.

cues.cue: vocabulary / take / years to master
models: One of the main causes of this is the fact that vocabulary takes years to master, and this leads to frustration among learners.

cues.cue: classroom time / limit / real conversation practice
models: This tends to occur because of classroom time limiting real conversation practice, which creates gaps in fluency, and over time these gaps become harder to close.

tasks.question: Why are people spending more time online these days?

cues.cue: online shopping / offer / convenience
models: The root cause of this is the sheer convenience of online shopping, which is why people spend more time online, and until this changes the trend will continue.

cues.cue: smartphones / make / access constant
models: This is mainly caused by smartphones making access constant, which means that people check their phones throughout the day, and as a result screen time keeps rising.

cues.cue: social media / reward / users with constant updates
models: This can largely be attributed to social media rewarding users with constant updates, since it keeps people engaged, which explains why sessions grow longer.

cues.cue: streaming services / offer / endless entertainment
models: One of the main causes of this is the fact that streaming services offer endless entertainment, and this leads people to spend hours online.

cues.cue: remote work / require / more screen time
models: This is primarily the result of remote work requiring more screen time, which has led to longer hours online, particularly during the working week.

cues.cue: apps / design / to keep users scrolling
models: A major contributing factor is the way apps are designed to keep users scrolling, and this has meant that time online keeps increasing.

tasks.question: Why do you think obesity is increasing in many countries?

cues.cue: diets / rely / on processed food
models: This is mainly caused by diets relying heavily on processed food, which means that people consume more calories than they need, and as a result obesity rates climb.

cues.cue: modern lifestyles / involve / less physical activity
models: This problem is frequently linked to modern lifestyles involving less physical activity, which suggests that people burn fewer calories, and therefore weight gain becomes more common.

cues.cue: fast food / become / cheap and widely available
models: This largely arises from the fact that fast food has become cheap and widely available, making it difficult for people to choose healthier options.

cues.cue: sugary drinks / add / hidden calories
models: The root cause of this is that sugary drinks add hidden calories to people's diets, which is why obesity keeps rising, and until this changes the trend will persist.

cues.cue: screen time / replace / outdoor exercise
models: This tends to occur because of screen time replacing outdoor exercise, which creates more sedentary habits, and over time this contributes to weight gain.

cues.cue: portion sizes / increase / over recent decades
models: One of the main causes of this is the fact that portion sizes have increased over recent decades, and this leads to higher calorie intake without people noticing.

tasks.question: Why do some students find exams so stressful?

cues.cue: exams / determine / future opportunities
models: This can largely be attributed to exams determining future opportunities, since so much is at stake, which explains why students feel anxious.

cues.cue: revision periods / compress / into short timeframes
models: This issue often stems from revision periods being compressed into short timeframes, which results in students feeling rushed and overwhelmed.

cues.cue: parents / place / high expectations on students
models: A major contributing factor is the way parents place high expectations on students, and this has meant that pressure builds well before the exam itself.

cues.cue: students / fear / letting themselves down
models: The root cause of this is that students fear letting themselves down, which is why the pressure feels so personal, and until this changes stress levels will stay high.

cues.cue: schools / rank / students by results
models: This problem is frequently linked to schools ranking students by results, which suggests that competition adds to the pressure, and therefore stress increases further.

cues.cue: sleep / suffer / during exam periods
models: This is primarily the result of sleep suffering during exam periods, which has led to poorer concentration, particularly in the final weeks before exams.

tasks.question: Why has fast food become so popular around the world?

cues.cue: fast food / offer / convenience and speed
models: This is mainly caused by fast food offering convenience and speed, which means that busy people can eat quickly, and as a result its popularity keeps growing.

cues.cue: fast food chains / advertise / aggressively
models: One of the main causes of this is the fact that fast food chains advertise aggressively, and this leads to strong brand recognition worldwide.

cues.cue: prices / stay / low compared to other meals
models: This largely arises from the fact that prices stay low compared to other meals, making it difficult for healthier alternatives to compete.

cues.cue: busy schedules / leave / little time to cook
models: This issue often stems from busy schedules leaving little time to cook, which results in people turning to fast food out of necessity.

cues.cue: globalisation / spread / Western food culture
models: This tends to occur because of globalisation spreading Western food culture, which creates demand in new markets, and over time fast food chains expand further.

cues.cue: fast food / taste / consistently appealing
models: A major contributing factor is the way fast food tastes consistently appealing, and this has meant that customers keep returning.
